title: Chapter 15. Krishnadasa, Kanu Dasa, Vasu Ghosha, Yadunandana, Nayanananda, Yadu, Ramananda, Chaitanyadasa: the rest of the "GPT only" group and finds of a full check of signatures
html:
This chapter completes the group of padas by the other poets (apart from Narahari) that are known from the "Gaura-pada-tarangini" (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), without the padas in nagari-bhava. It contains padas missed by earlier checks (in the OCR text of GPT1 some headings "N pada" lack the danda, and such padas merged with their neighbours) and finds of a full manual re-check of the signatures of all contemporary poets throughout GPT1. Four of the finds turned out not to be "GPT only": they are in the "Padakalpataru" (PK 2099 — Yadunandana, PK 2101 — Yadu, also in the "Bhakti-ratnakara", PK 2083 — unsigned, PK 1867 — Chaitanyadasa); there the text is given from PK with the readings of GPT. The padas follow the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura-avatara, Advaita's call and the Lord's appearance, goshtha-bhava and the kirtanas of Navadvipa, Shachi's lament after the sannyasa, the Lord's bhavas in Puri, Nityananda. The language of some padas (nos. 1, 3–5, 14) has New Bengali forms — by these they are probably late; Majumdar in general considers GPT unreliable for attribution. Hence the attribution of padas known only from GPT is conditional (C, the late ones included: late language alone does not indicate a forgery). The Bengali original, variant readings and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Krishnadasa — "āre re ninduka bhāi…" (GPT1 p. 14, no. 35)

Rebuke of a blasphemer: Gauranga is the essence of all avataras; when drunkenness, killing of the unborn and debauchery under the guise of tantric religion had overrun Bharata and people had begun to worship yakshas, rakshasas and Vishahari, Sri Chaitanya appeared in Navadvipa, gave everyone the name of Hari, saved Jagai and Madhai, united brahmanas with yavanas; whoever does not believe this has no deliverance. Raga dhanashi.1

আরে রে নিন্দুক ভাই তোর কি রে বোধ নাই বৃথাই ধরিলা দোন আঁখি ।
সব অবতারসার শ্রীগৌরাঙ্গ অবতার তুমি তাহে রৈয়াছ উপেখি ॥

āre re ninduka bhāi tora ki re bodha nāi bṛthāi dharilā dona ām̐khi |
saba abatārasāra śrīgaurāṅga abatāra tumi tāhe raiyācha upekhi ||

āre re — hey; ninduka bhāi — brother blasphemer; tora ki re bodha nāi — have you no understanding; bṛthāi — in vain; dharilā — you bear; dona ām̐khi — a pair of eyes; saba abatāra-sāra — the essence of all avataras; śrī-gaurāṅga abatāra — the avatara of Sri Gauranga; tumi tāhe — you Him; raiyācha upekhi — disregard

1.1"Hey, brother blasphemer, have you no understanding at all? In vain you bear a pair of eyes! The essence of all avataras is the avatara of Sri Gauranga — and you pass Him by with disregard.

সুরাপান অত্যাচার ভ্রূণহত্যা ব্যভিচার তন্ত্রধর্মে ভারত ব্যাপিল ।
যক্ষ রক্ষ বিষহরি নানা উপহার করি জীব সবে পূজিতে লাগিল ॥

surāpāna atyācāra bhrūṇahatyā byabhicāra tantradharme bhārata byāpila |
yakṣa rakṣa biṣahari nānā upahāra kari jība sabe pūjite lāgila ||

surāpāna — drunkenness; atyācāra — violence; bhrūṇahatyā — killing of the unborn; byabhicāra — debauchery; tantra-dharme — under the guise of tantric religion; bhārata byāpila — overran Bharata; yakṣa rakṣa — yakshas, rakshasas; biṣahari — Vishahari (Manasa); nānā upahāra kari — with various offerings; jība sabe — all people; pūjite lāgila — began to worship

1.2Drunkenness, violence, killing of the unborn, debauchery — under the guise of tantric religion they overran Bharata; yakshas, rakshasas and Vishahari people began to worship with all kinds of offerings.2

দেখিয়া জীবের দৈন্য প্রভু মোর শ্রীচৈতন্য নবদ্বীপে প্রকট হইলা ।
তারক ব্রহ্ম হরিনাম যাচি সবে করি দান ধর্মের সে গ্লানি ঘুচাইলা ॥

dekhiyā jībera dainya prabhu mora śrīcaitanya nabadvīpe prakaṭa hailā |
tāraka brahma harināma yāci sabe kari dāna dharmera se glāni ghucāilā ||

dekhiyā — seeing; jībera dainya — the misery of the living beings; prabhu mora śrī-caitanya — my Lord Sri Chaitanya; nabadvīpe — in Navadvipa; prakaṭa hailā — appeared; tāraka brahma — the saving taraka-brahma; hari-nāma — the name of Hari; yāci — offering unasked; sabe kari dāna — giving to all; dharmera se glāni — that decline of dharma; ghucāilā — removed

1.3Seeing the misery of the living beings, my Lord Sri Chaitanya appeared in Navadvipa: the saving name of Hari — the taraka-brahma — He Himself offered and gave to all, and removed the decline of dharma.3

জগাই মাধাই আদি দুষ্কৃতের নিরবধি হরিনামে করিলা উদ্ধার ।
ব্রাহ্মণ যবনে মিলি করাইলা কোলাকুলি পরতেকে দেখ একবার ॥

jagāi mādhāi ādi duṣkṛtera nirabadhi harināme karilā uddhāra |
brāhmaṇa yabane mili karāilā kolākuli parateke dekha ekabāra ||

jagāi mādhāi ādi — Jagai, Madhai and others; duṣkṛtera nirabadhi — doing evil without end; hari-nāme — by the name of Hari; karilā uddhāra — saved; brāhmaṇa yabane mili — uniting brahmanas with yavanas; karāilā kolākuli — made them embrace; parateke — with your own eyes; dekha ekabāra — see but once

1.4Jagai, Madhai and others who did evil without end He saved by the name of Hari;
He united brahmanas and yavanas — made them embrace: see it with your own eyes but once!

নাস্তিকে করিলা ভক্ত খঞ্জে কৈলা গতিশক্ত অন্ধের করিলা চক্ষুদান ।
কহে দীন কৃষ্ণদাস নহিলে ইথে বিশ্বাস তোর আর নাহি পরিত্রাণ ॥

nāstike karilā bhakta khañje kailā gatiśakta andhera karilā cakṣudāna |
kahe dīna kṛṣṇadāsa nahile ithe biśvāsa tora āra nāhi paritrāṇa ||

nāstike — atheists; karilā bhakta — made devotees; khañje — the lame; kailā gati-śakta — made able to walk; andhera — to the blind; karilā cakṣu-dāna — gave sight; kahe dīna kṛṣṇadāsa — says lowly Krishnadasa; nahile ithe biśvāsa — if there is no faith in this; tora āra nāhi paritrāṇa — there is no more deliverance for you

1.5He made atheists into devotees, gave the lame the power to walk, granted the blind their sight." Says lowly Krishnadasa: if you do not believe this, there is no more deliverance for you.4

GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 35. The pada is not in PK, the "Bhakti-ratnakara" (BR), the "Kshanada-gita-chintamani" (KGC) or the "Padamrita-samudra" (PS); it was missing from the catalogue (new row KR-022). Under the signature "Krishnadasa" PK has 22 padas by different poets. The denunciation of "tantric religion" and words like "killing of the unborn" (bhrūṇahatyā) point to a late origin (18th–19th c.); C. Vishahari (CB Adi 2). Vishahari is Manasa, the goddess of snakes. "Tantric religion" here means the rites with wine and the like that the poet denounces. "Kali-santarana Upanishad" calls the destroyer of the taint of Kali. "Decline of dharma" echoes Bhagavad-gita 4.7–8. thus Haridasa Thakura, born in a Muslim family, was one of His closest associates (CB Adi 16); the Kazi became His devotee (CC Adi 17).

2. Krishnadasa — "śāntipurera buṛāmālī…" (GPT1 pp. 14–15, no. 36)

An allegory of the tree of Chaitanya: the old gardener of Shantipur (Advaita) brought a seedling from the garden of Vaikuntha and gave it to the gardener Nitai; in Nadia grew the tree of Chaitanya and bore two fruits — the Name and prema; Nitai gives them out to all, down to chandalas and yavanas, whether they wish it or not; the poet laments that he did not see that tree and did not know the merciful gardener. Raga suhai.5

শান্তিপুরের বুড়ামালী বৈকুণ্ঠ বাগান খালি করিয়া আনিল এক চারা ।
নিতাই মালীরে পাঞা চারা তার হাতে দিয়া যতনে রোপিতে কৈল নাড়া ॥

śāntipurera buṛāmālī baikuṇṭha bāgāna khāli kariyā ānila eka cārā |
nitāi mālīre pāñā cārā tāra hāte diyā yatane ropite kaila nāṛā ||

śāntipurera — of Shantipur; buṛā-mālī — the old gardener; baikuṇṭha bāgāna khāli kariyā — emptying the garden of Vaikuntha; ānila eka cārā — brought a seedling; nitāi mālīre pāñā — finding the gardener Nitai; cārā tāra hāte diyā — putting the seedling in his hands; yatane ropite — to plant with care; kaila nāṛā — said Nara (Advaita)

2.1The old gardener of Shantipur, emptying the garden of Vaikuntha, brought a single seedling; finding the gardener Nitai, He put the seedling into His hands — "Plant it with care," said Nara.6

নদীয়া উত্তম স্থান তাহাতে করি উদ্যান রোপিল চৈতন্য-তরু মালী ।
বাড়ে তরু দিনে দিনে শাখাপত্র অগণনে গজাইল যত্নে জল ঢালি ॥

nadīyā uttama sthāna tāhāte kari udyāna ropila caitanya-taru mālī |
bāṛe taru dine dine śākhāpatra agaṇane gajāila yatne jala ḍhāli ||

nadīyā uttama sthāna — Nadia is the finest place; tāhāte kari udyāna — laying out a garden there; ropila caitanya-taru mālī — the gardener planted the tree of Chaitanya; bāṛe taru dine dine — the tree grows day by day; śākhā-patra agaṇane — branches and leaves past counting; gajāila — brought up; yatne jala ḍhāli — watering with care

2.2Nadia is the finest place: laying out a garden there, the gardener planted the tree of Chaitanya; the tree grows day by day, its branches and leaves past counting: watering it with care, He brought it up.

পাইয়া ভকতি-জল নাম-প্রেম দুই ফল প্রসবিল সে তরু সুন্দর ।
সেই দুই ফলের আশে জীব-পাখী নিত্য আসে কোলাহল করে নিরন্তর ॥

pāiyā bhakati-jala nāma-prema dui phala prasabila se taru sundara |
sei dui phalera āśe jība-pākhī nitya āse kolāhala kare nirantara ||

pāiyā bhakati-jala — receiving the water of bhakti; nāma-prema dui phala — two fruits, the Name and prema; prasabila — bore; se taru sundara — that beautiful tree; sei dui phalera āśe — in hope of those two fruits; jība-pākhī — the birds, the living beings; nitya āse — come daily; kolāhala kare nirantara — chatter without cease

2.3Receiving the water of bhakti, the beautiful tree bore two fruits — the Name and prema; in hope of these two fruits the birds — the living beings — come every day and chatter without cease.

আনন্দে নিতাই মালী লইয়া মাথায় ডালি দুই ফল সবারে বিলায় ।
নাই জাতি-ভেদাভেদ সবার মিটিল খেদ ফলাস্বাদ সকলেতে পায় ॥

ānande nitāi mālī laiyā māthāya ḍāli dui phala sabāre bilāya |
nāi jāti-bhedābheda sabāra miṭila kheda phalāsvāda sakalete pāya ||

ānande — joyfully; nitāi mālī — the gardener Nitai; laiyā māthāya ḍāli — a basket on his head; dui phala sabāre bilāya — gives out the two fruits to all; nāi jāti-bhedābheda — there is no distinction of caste; sabāra miṭila kheda — everyone's sorrow is gone; phalāsvāda sakalete pāya — each gets the taste of the fruit

2.4The joyful gardener Nitai, a basket on His head, gives out the two fruits to all; there is no distinction of caste — everyone's sorrow is gone: each one gets the taste of the fruit.

ধর লও লও বলি আনন্দে নিতাই মালী আচণ্ডালে ফল বিলাইল ।
যেই চায় সেই পায় যে না চাহে সেও পায় যবনেও ফল আস্বাদিল ॥

dhara lao lao bali ānande nitāi mālī ācaṇḍāle phala bilāila |
yei cāya sei pāya ye nā cāhe seo pāya yabaneo phala āsvādila ||

dhara lao lao bali — crying "Hold, take, take!"; ācaṇḍāle — down to the chandalas; phala bilāila — gave out the fruits; yei cāya sei pāya — whoever asks receives; ye nā cāhe seo pāya — whoever does not ask receives too; yabaneo — even the yavanas; phala āsvādila — tasted the fruit

2.5"Hold it, take it, take it!" — crying out, the joyful gardener Nitai gave out the fruits down to the chandalas; whoever asks receives, whoever does not ask receives too: even the yavanas tasted the fruit.7

কি মোর করম ফেরে না হেরিনু সে তরুরে না চিনিনু সে মালী দয়াল ।
কৃষ্ণদাস দুরাশয় দন্তে তৃণ ধরি কয় ধিক্ ধিক্ এ পোড়া কপাল ॥

ki mora karama phere nā herinu se tarure nā cininu se mālī dayāla |
kṛṣṇadāsa durāśaya dante tṛṇa dhari kaya dhik dhik e poṛā kapāla ||

ki mora karama phere — what a turn of my karma; nā herinu se tarure — I did not see that tree; nā cininu — did not know; se mālī dayāla — that merciful gardener; kṛṣṇadāsa durāśaya — Krishnadasa, full of bad desires; dante tṛṇa dhari kaya — holding a straw in his teeth, says; dhik dhik — shame, shame; e poṛā kapāla — on this burnt fate

2.6What a turn of my karma: I did not see that tree, I did not know that merciful gardener! Krishnadasa, full of bad desires, holding a straw between his teeth, says: shame, shame on my wretched fate!

BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row KR-023). Date of composition not established; attribution by GPT (C). is also the gardener; the first sprout is Madhavendra Puri (CC Adi 9); here the allegory is different: the seedling is brought by Advaita, who called the Lord down, and the gardener is Nityananda, who gives out the fruits. between the teeth" is a sign of complete humility.

3. Kanu Dasa — "ekadina kamalākṣa kana haridāse…" (GPT1 p. 448, no. 32)

Advaita (Kamalaksha) says to Haridasa: many years have passed, and the hope with which He came to earth is not fulfilled; the Lord of Vaikuntha Himself told Him that He would descend to earth for the sake of the suffering living beings and bade Him come before Him; can the Lord's promise be in vain? The poet: the Lord never speaks untruth — He will surely appear. Raga dhanashi.8

একদিন কমলাক্ষ কন হরিদাসে ।
আইলাম অবনীতে যেই অভিলাষে ॥

ekadina kamalākṣa kana haridāse |
āilāma abanīte yei abhilāṣe ||

ekadina — one day; kamalākṣa — Kamalaksha (Advaita); kana haridāse — says to Haridasa; āilāma abanīte — I came to earth; yei abhilāṣe — with which desire

3.1One day Kamalaksha says to Haridasa:
"The wish with which I came to earth —

বহু বর্ষ গত হৈল না পূরিল আশ ।
সাধনা বিফল ভেল হইনু নৈরাশ ॥

bahu barṣa gata haila nā pūrila āśa |
sādhanā biphala bhela hainu nairāśa ||

bahu barṣa gata haila — many years have passed; nā pūrila āśa — the hope is unfulfilled; sādhanā biphala bhela — the austerity has been fruitless; hainu nairāśa — I am in despair

3.2many years have passed, and the hope is unfulfilled:
my austerity is fruitless, I am in despair.

বৈকুণ্ঠবিহারী মোরে কৈলা নিজ মুখে ।
পাপভারাক্রান্ত মহী জীব কাঁদে দুখে ॥

baikuṇṭhabihārī more kailā nija mukhe |
pāpabhārākrānta mahī jība kām̐de dukhe ||

baikuṇṭha-bihārī — the Lord (lit. "One who sports") of Vaikuntha; more kailā — told me; nija mukhe — with His own lips; pāpa-bhārākrānta mahī — the earth burdened with sins; jība kām̐de dukhe — the living beings weep in sorrow

3.3The Lord of Vaikuntha with His own lips told me:
'The earth is burdened with sins, the living beings weep in sorrow;

জীবদুখ নাশিবারে যাইব অবনী ।
অগ্রে পদার্পণ তথা করহ আপনি ॥

jībadukha nāśibāre yāiba abanī |
agre padārpaṇa tathā karaha āpani ||

jība-dukha nāśibāre — to destroy the sorrow of the living beings; yāiba abanī — I shall go to earth; agre — first; padārpaṇa tathā karaha — set foot there; āpani — You Yourself

3.4to destroy the sorrow of the living beings I shall descend to earth;
You Yourself set foot there before Me.'

প্রভুর সে অঙ্গীকার বুঝি ব্যর্থ হৈল ।
মোর দ্বারে জীবদুঃখ বুঝি না ঘুচিল ॥

prabhura se aṅgīkāra bujhi byartha haila |
mora dvāre jībaduḥkha bujhi nā ghucila ||

prabhura se aṅgīkāra — that promise of the Lord; bujhi — can it be; byartha haila — has proved vain; mora dvāre — through me; jība-duḥkha — the sorrow of the living beings; bujhi nā ghucila — will it not be removed

3.5Can that promise of the Lord have proved vain?
Will the sorrow of the living beings not be removed through me?"9

কানু কহে মিথ্যাবাদী পহুঁ কভু নয় ।
অবশ্য জীবের ভাগ্যে হইবা উদয় ॥

kānu kahe mithyābādī pahum̐ kabhu naya |
abaśya jībera bhāgye haibā udaya ||

kānu kahe — says Kanu; mithyābādī — one who speaks untruth; pahum̐ kabhu naya — the Lord never is; abaśya — surely; jībera bhāgye — by the good fortune of the living beings; haibā udaya — He will appear

3.6Says Kanu: the Lord never speaks untruth —
by the good fortune of the living beings He will surely appear.

or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new row KD-012). Signature "Kanu" (kānu); Kanu Thakura, the son of Purushottama, is a poet of the next generation, and the language of the pada (sādhanā biphala, pāpabhārākrānta) is New Bengali: the pada is probably late; C. Kamalaksha is Advaita's childhood name. is not ignorance but compassion for the living beings and longing for the Lord's appearance, expressed in lila. The conversation of the Lord with Advaita in Vaikuntha that is spoken of here is not described in CC or CB; CC (Adi 3) speaks of Advaita's resolve to call Krishna by worship with Ganga water and tulasi. Haridasa Thakura came to Advaita in Shantipur (CB Adi 16).

4. Kanu Dasa — "cauddaśata sāta śāke…" (GPT1 p. 449, no. 33)

The Lord's appearance: in the year 1407 of the Shaka era, on the full moon of Phalguna, during a lunar eclipse, Advaita Acharya was offering tulasi leaves to the Ganga; suddenly He leapt up with a thundering cry and broke into a dance: "I have brought, I have brought Gaura to Nadia!" — and Haridasa understood that Gauranga had been born. Raga dhanashi.10

চৌদ্দশত সাত শাকে পূর্ণিমা দিবসে ।
চন্দ্রগ্রহণের কালে ফাল্গুনের মাসে ॥

cauddaśata sāta śāke pūrṇimā dibase |
candragrahaṇera kāle phālgunera māse ||

cauddaśata sāta śāke — in Shaka fourteen hundred and seven; pūrṇimā dibase — on the day of the full moon; candra-grahaṇera kāle — at the time of the lunar eclipse; phālgunera māse — in the month of Phalguna

4.1In the year fourteen hundred and seven of the Shaka era, on the day of the full moon,
at the time of the lunar eclipse, in the month of Phalguna,

অদ্বৈত আচার্য প্রভু ভক্তিযুক্ত মনে ।
গঙ্গাতে তুলসী পত্র করিছে প্রদানে ॥

advaita ācārya prabhu bhaktiyukta mane |
